Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172 asserting that on 17.05.2024 at about 9.50 p.m. when riding a Scooter bearing No.KA-02-KW-3766 on Nagarabhavi main road, near Stories junction, right turn area, driver of a Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172, drove the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the Shanthakumar R vs Vandana V on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93886397/
1 same to motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

2. Petitioner took treatment at G.M. Hospital, Nagarabhavi by spending Rs.1,50,000/-, as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 48 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/-p.m. by working as Cable operator.

3. Regarding accident Jnanabharathi Traffic police registered crime No.135/2024 against the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172.
4.

In response to the notice respondents No.2 appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident nature and consequences of injuries suffered by petitioner.
5. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1- owner of the car remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 19.12.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 17.05.2024 at about 9.50 p.m. on Nagarabhavi main road, near Stories junction, in view of the negligent use of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04- ND-6172 car dashed to the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KW-3766, thereby accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner, rider of the motorcycle?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?

If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 05.02.2025 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 15 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15.

On 04.03.2025, 18.03.2025 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW2 and get produced 2 documents at Ex.P.16 and P.17.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.5,12,162/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-

sentences.text: Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 17.05.2024 at about 9.50 p.m. when riding a Scooter bearing No.KA-02-KW-3766 on Nagarabhavi main road, near Stories junction right turn area, driver of a Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172, drove the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion that at the time of alleged accident there was heavy traffic in the place of accident.
PW1 admitted that during alleged accident he was turning his two wheeler from east- west direction towards north side.
PW1 admitted that the place of accident is a junction area and the car came from Kengunte side towards Nammora Thindi Hotel (80 feet road).
PW1 denied the suggestion that even after noticing the appearance of the car, he turned the motorcycle towards right side thereby became the reason for the accident.

PW1 denied the suggestion that as per Spot Mahazar and sketch due to his sole negligence riding of the motorcycle the accident taken place and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
13. In the evidence PW.2- Dr. Nagaraj B.N. stated nothing about the reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.135/2024 registered on 18.05.2024 by Jnanabharathi Traffic police against Tejas- driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC on the basis of the complaint/statement of the petitioner- Shanthakumar recorded in the hospital.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of statement of the petitioner recorded in the hospital.

Ex.P.3 is the police intimation dated 17.05.2024 forwarded by GM Hospital, Bengaluru to PSI, Jnanabharathi Traffic Police station, Bengaluru in which reason for the injuries noted as alleged history of road traffic accident 2 - wheeler v/s 4- wheeler, patient was on 2-wheeler, on 17.05.2024 at 9.50 p.m., Nagarabhavi main road, Opposite to Swathi Hotel ring view.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of the wound certificate issued by GM hospitals.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of the motor vehicle accident report.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Jnanabharathi Traffic police in crime No.135/2024 against Tejas S. S/o Somashekaraiah- driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC.
15.
In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the contents of the police records and oral evidence of PW1 regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 17.05.2024 at about 9.50 p.m. when petitioner was riding a Scooter bearing No.KA-02-KW-3766 on Nagarabhavi main road, near Stories junction, right turn area, Tejas S. S/o Somashekaraiah- driver of a Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172, drove the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to motorcycle, thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 Accordingly.
16. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered GA Type 3/3 distal tibia fibula fracture, took treatment at GM hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 17.05.2024 Shanthakumar R vs Vandana V on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93886397/
3 to 21.05.2024 and from 09.06.2024 to 12.06.2024, underwent surgery by spending Rs.2,31,976/-.

Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.25,000/-p.m. by working as Cable Connector (Cable operator).
17.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
18. In the cross-examination PW.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of incident neither worked as Cable collector (connector) nor earned Rs.25,000/- per month.
PW1 admitted lack of documents regarding his occupation and income.
PW1 denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.2,31,976/- towards treatment.

19. In the evidence PW.2- Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon stated that on 03.03.2025 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 48% to left lower limb which is about 16% to the whole body.
In the evidence PW.2 produced Clinical examination report dated 03.03.2025 and X-rays at Ex.P.16 and P.17.
In the cross- examination PW.2 admitted that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified inpatient treatment record of the petitioner.
PW.2 stated that as on 03.03.2025 fractures of the petitioner are mal-united and as per information provided by the petitioner, petitioner is a cable technician.
PW2 admitted that as on 03.03.2025 petitioner can perform work in hands.

20. Wound certificate, Discharge summary, X-rays and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered abrasion over the left elbow, medial malleolus of left leg, puncture wound with deformity of left leg, lower 1/3rd with exposed bone, fracture of distal tibia and fibula,
took treatment at GM Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 17.05.2024 to 21.05.2024 and from 09.06.2024 to 12.06.2024.
21.
In the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9 the date of birth of PW1 is noted as 17.05.1977.
In the copy of DL and Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.12 and P.13 the date birth of the petitioner (PW1) is noted as 16.01.1976.
The medical bills shows that petitioner has spent Rs.2,25,162/- towards treatment charges.
22. In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding his occupation and quantum of income.
In this case petitioner has not produced any evidence to show either decrease in the income or loss of income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.
Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.2 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. is not sufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent functional Disability).

23. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of the petitioner, I award Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.2,25,162/- towards medical expenses, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.1,32,000/-
(16,500 x8) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.60,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.

sentences.text: Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.5,12,162/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Sl. No.
Head of Compensation Amount/
Rs 1. Pain and sufferings 80,000-00 2.

Medical expenses 2,25,162-00 3. Attendant conveyance and 15,000-00 nourishment charges 4. Loss of income during 1,32,000-00 treatment period 5. Loss of amenities and future 60,000-00 unhappiness Total 5,12,162-00 25.

In the written statement, respondent No.2 admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172 as on the date of accident issued by respondent No.2- insurance company.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.1 - owner of the Car has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.5,12,162/- (Rupees five lakh twelve thousand one hundred sixty two only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-ND-6172 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 7th day of May, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
